transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. It's very nice to meet you too. I, uh, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. 

Well, I suppose what brings me in is... I've just been a little, I don't know, scatterbrained lately. Nothing too terrible, I don't think! But... well, I keep forgetting things that I really shouldn’t. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. Like, um, slipping up on my heart follow-up appointments, or forgetting to call the clinic back when I'm supposed to. And I like to do little repair jobs just to keep busy, but lately I keep showing up to do them and realizing I didn't even bring the right tools. 

It's just a bit silly of me, I suppose. Does that make sense? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to talk to you about it.
Because of the forgetting, are you needing help with your usual day-to-day tasks that you used to handle on your own?

Oh, no, no, I wouldn't say I need a caretaker or anything drastic like that! I can still manage the house and feed myself just fine, I promise. I hope I didn't make it sound worse than it is. 

But, um... well, I suppose I do rely on others a bit more to catch my mistakes lately. It's just... well, it’s gotten to where the senior-center repair group can’t really count on me the way they used to, which I feel just awful about. I hate letting them down when I'm supposed to be helping. And my regular doctor’s office, they've had to chase me around a bit about those missed heart follow-ups. I really hate being a nuisance to the nurses there, having them call to remind me. 

So, I guess I am dropping the ball a little bit when I'm left entirely to my own devices... is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
Compared with how you used to be, do you feel your memory and thinking have clearly gotten worse?

Oh, goodness, no. I really wouldn't say it's clearly gotten worse. I hope I didn't give you the impression that my mind is going! 

I feel like my thinking is still perfectly fine, honestly. I've sort of always been someone who... well, who jumps into things a bit fast, you know? Always on the go, always moving, maybe not pausing to double-check my pockets before I run out the door. So being a little scattered and rushing into things isn't exactly a brand-new trait for me. 

I don't think my memory is actually failing or anything scary like that. Just a few silly slip-ups here and there. That's fairly normal, don't you think? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here and not making a mountain out of a molehill.
Have you been told by a doctor that you have any brain-related medical condition, such as a stroke or Parkinson’s disease?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I haven't had any strokes or... or Parkinson's, or anything serious with my brain. My doctor has never mentioned anything along those lines, thank heavens. 

I'm perfectly healthy in that department, I promise! Just a bit of a scattered fellow sometimes, like I said. I hope you don't think I'm wasting your time by coming in when it's nothing major like a stroke. I just wanted to be thorough, you know? Did I answer that right for you?
